precepts.text: Sychar was near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph; a parcel of land and an inheritance are one and the same.
precepts.point: Boaz bought all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's and Mahlon's, and purchased Ruth to be his wife to raise up the name of the dead, that it be not cut off from among his brethren.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Ruth 4 is a trial at the gate before ten elders over land. Elimelech had land; he died, and his two sons, Mahlon and Chilion, died too, leaving no man to take it. So the land had to be taken up by the next of kin. Boaz told the nearer kinsman that Naomi “selleth a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech’s.” A parcel of land: that phrase opens the whole chapter.

John 4 uses the same wording. Christ “must needs go through Samaria. Then cometh he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.” Jacob gave Joseph that parcel of ground; he bought his son that land.

A parcel of land, a parcel of ground, a parcel of a field: they are all the same thing, and a parcel of land and an inheritance are one and the same. So when Boaz bought the parcel that was Elimelech's, he was not making an ordinary purchase. He was taking up an inheritance in Israel, one that had to stay in the family of the dead.

precepts.text: Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth. That is the truth in spirit and truth: the keeping of God's commandments.
precepts.point: God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth. There is one word there I want you to emphasise. Must. There is no other way to do it. You must worship him in spirit and truth, which is the application of God's laws.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

precepts.why:
Hosea prophesied: “Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.” These are those days. We were out for a long time, without the understanding of who we were as a people or what the will of God was for us, and in the last days the Lord raised up the prophets on the earth again to teach the word of God and apply it, so we could be delivered out of here. Where in the New Testament do we read that the children of Israel will return and seek the Lord? Right here: “But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeketh such to worship him.” That's us, reviving in this time. What you are part of is the resurrection of God's Christ's kingdom, and in that kingdom righteousness must reign. The Father is going to try us to see if we will worship him according to spirit and truth.

And what is the truth? “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” Worshipping in truth is the application of God's laws, the keeping of God's commandments.

“God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.” Emphasise one word: must. There's no other way to do it. Take one law that is not negotiable: remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy. We must congregate, it's a holy convocation; we cannot cook, clean, shop, buy or sell on the Lord's Sabbath. There's no deciding it's not important. It's those small things, the application of God's laws, that separate us. If someone won't congregate with the body and goes to congregate with somebody put out of the body, that's sin: can two walk together except they be agreed? We rationalize in our mind what we think God will be all right with, but his thoughts are not our thoughts. Do what he told you to do.

Where the law is not applied, Hosea says the Lord has a controversy with the land, “because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.” There is no knowledge of God because the laws of God are not being taught or enforced. “By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood.” To break out is to break away from the law: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” Blood touching blood is violence and hatred against each other. “Therefore shall the land mourn”: if those same sins abide in the body, the congregation won't grow or flourish. So leaders must teach the laws, hold people accountable to them, and be the example themselves. What God asks is a small thing next to the sins we have committed: not stealing, not swearing, not lying, not committing adultery, keeping the Sabbath holy. The truth is all we've got to get out of here. There is no plan B; outside of this is death.

precepts.text: This is Christ speaking to the Samaritan woman. Our fathers worshipped in this mountain: which was Mount Gerizim. And ye say that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship: y'all Jews say that. Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father. Why? Because 70 AD was coming; Rome was going to destroy all the remaining Israelites. Ye worship ye know not what: you, northern kingdom, don't understand what you're worshipping, cuz the northern kingdom went into idolatry. We know what we worship, for salvation is of the Jews: salvation comes from Judah. What was he letting her know? The temple was going to be destroyed, Israelites go into captivity, and you're going to have to deal with the Lord one on one. No more priests intervening for you.
precepts.point: The Lord God hath sworn by himself, I abhor the excellency of Jacob: because all 12 tribes was going off. Therefore will I deliver up the city with all that is therein. So the southern kingdom was going to get it, and the northern kingdom.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Amos set Zion and the mountain of Samaria against each other, and Christ speaks to the same divide with the Samaritan woman. “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”: that was Mount Gerizim. “and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship”: y’all Jews say that.

“Jesus saith unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father.” Why? Because 70 AD was coming; Rome was going to destroy all the remaining Israelites.

“Ye worship ye know not what”: you, northern kingdom, don’t understand what you are worshipping, because the northern kingdom went into idolatry. “we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews.” Salvation comes from Judah.

What was he letting her know? The temple was going to be destroyed, the Israelites would go into captivity, and you would have to deal with the Lord one on one, with no more priests intervening for you: “the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth”. Neither Samaria’s mountain nor Zion would stand; both houses would go captive, as Amos said.

precepts.text: Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone. Cuz remember, Jeroboam set up priests in the land. So we did not deal with them.
precepts.point: And many of the Samaritans of that city believed on him, and he abode there two days. If they weren't Israelites, why would he stay there and teach them for two days? It makes no sense. Now we believe, not because of thy saying: for we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world: of the world of Israel.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
After Christ dealt with Judah, “he must needs go through Samaria.” There the woman said, “How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” The southern kingdom did not deal with the northern kingdom. Remember the rift from Rehoboam; that was always the problem.

Hosea gives the reason: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” Remember, Jeroboam set up priests in the land, and Ephraim went into idolatry. So we did not deal with them.

But she was still an Israelite: “Art thou greater than our father Jacob”? Right there she's telling you she's an Israelite. People on YouTube say she wasn't, because Shalmaneser put men of Babylon and the Chaldees in the land, but there is more history: Ezra shows Israelites coming back to the land. And if she was lying about her identity, why didn't Christ correct her? He did correct her about something, her five husbands, letting her know she was living a whorish lifestyle, because sex does not constitute marriage. But he never corrected her nationality.

He revealed himself to her, “I that speak unto thee am he”, which he would not do if she were not an Israelite, and his disciples marvelled that he talked with her, because the Jews had no dealings with the Samaritans. Then he abode there two days teaching them, and they knew he was “the Saviour of the world”, the world of Israel. The one Hosea said to let alone, Christ went to gather.

precepts.text: And the head of Ephraim is Samaria. Samaria was the capital for Ephraim.
precepts.point: And many of the Samaritans of that city believed on him, and he abode there two days. If they weren't Israelites, why would he stay there and teach them for two days? It makes no sense. Now we believe, not because of thy saying: for we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world: of the world of Israel.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Why is a woman of Samaria an Israelite, and why did the Jews have no dealings with her? Isaiah names it: “And the head of Ephraim is Samaria”. Samaria was the capital of Ephraim, the head city of the northern kingdom.

So when John says Christ “must needs go through Samaria” and met “a woman of Samaria”, he is in the land of Ephraim, among the northern kingdom. That is why she could say “our father Jacob, which gave us the well”, and “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”. Her fathers were the fathers of Israel.

The rift between the kingdoms went back to Rehoboam, and Judah had nothing to do with Ephraim and its capital. But Christ said “the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father”, the hour of 70 AD, when nobody would be worshipping in Jerusalem or Samaria. “Ye worship ye know not what: we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews.” He stayed two days in Samaria and many believed on him. That is the raising up of the tabernacle of David that fell: both houses gathered back to the Messiah.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
Christ says he is “the life.” He tells the woman at the well: “But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.”

He is that sustenance again. Just as he said, “he that believeth on me shall never thirst”, he is the water as well as the bread. Remember in 1 Corinthians 10 it says they all ate the same spiritual meat and all drank of that same spiritual drink, from the spiritual rock in the wilderness.

The water out of the rock physically happened so that they could live, and so that we could have its meaning today. The water Christ gives becomes a well inside you, springing up into everlasting life. That is why he is the life.

precepts.point: Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst, but it shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life. note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
The woman of Samaria said, “How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” These Samaritans were Israelites who still lived there. Samaria is north of Jerusalem, as the map shows, and the Jews of Jerusalem stopped dealing with our people located in Samaria.

Why did that happen? A brother answered from Hosea: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” That is why she said it. The scripture said Ephraim was joined to idols, and the word was to let him alone.

So the separation between the Jews and the Samaritans was not just a grudge; it grew out of the judgment on the northern kingdom for its idolatry. Judah took that word and left Ephraim alone. Yet here Christ, of Judah, sits at Jacob's well and asks a woman of Samaria to give him drink.

precepts.text: Call her name Loruhamah: for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel. They fully went into idolatry. Call his name Loammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God. That was the message to the northern kingdom because of their idolatry. But then it comes back: in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God. What is he saying? I am going to bring you back together again. All the prophets spoke from a place of prophecy, judgment, and eventually redemption. That is what gives us hope to repent: if there were no endgame where we come out of this, there is no incentive.
precepts.point: Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst, but it shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life. The water, the understanding he was going to give her, would bring about the kingdom and salvation for them, because they were disconnected from it for so long.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Hosea shows why Ephraim was let alone. “Call her name Lo–ruhamah: for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away.” He would no longer have mercy on the house of Israel, because they fully went into idolatry. “But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save them by the Lord their God, and will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, by horses, nor by horsemen”, as can be read in 2 Kings 19.

“Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” That was the message to the northern kingdom because of his anger at their idolatry: you will not be my people, and I will not be your God. That is why the woman said the Jews have no dealings with us.

But then it comes back: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” What is he saying? I am going to bring you back together again.

All the prophets spoke from a place of prophecy, judgment, and eventually redemption. That is what gives us hope to change and repent. If there were no endgame where we come out of this, there would be no incentive. But God said if you turn back to me, in the place where it was said you are not my people, there you will be called the sons of God.

precepts.text: Within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken. It was already prophesied: God already told them that in 65 years the northern kingdom would be destroyed, and that is what Hosea 1 is recording.
precepts.point: Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst, but it shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life. The water, the understanding he was going to give her, would bring about the kingdom and salvation for them, because they were disconnected from it for so long.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Before Hosea recorded the Lord casting off the house of Israel, Isaiah had already prophesied it: “For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.”

They already knew. God already told them that within sixty-five years Ephraim, the northern kingdom, would be broken and destroyed, and that is what Hosea 1 is recording: Lo–ruhamah, no more mercy on the house of Israel, and Lo–ammi, ye are not my people.

So when the woman of Samaria says the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans, she is standing at the end of that prophecy. Ephraim was broken “that it be not a people”, cut off for idolatry. And that is exactly why it matters that Christ, a Jew, is speaking to her at Jacob's well: the people who were broken off are about to be offered the living water.

precepts.text: A brother answered what the living water is: that he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word. The living water is the word of God, the understanding that the tribes were going to be gathered back together.
precepts.point: Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst, but it shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life. The water, the understanding he was going to give her, would bring about the kingdom and salvation for them, because they were disconnected from it for so long.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Christ told her, “If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.” What is the living water? A brother answered from Ephesians: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word”.

You are cleansed by the washing of water by the word, so the living water is the word of God. What Christ would have given her was understanding: the understanding that the tribes were going to be gathered back together again.

She said, “Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well”? That shows she understood she was part of the twelve tribes of Israel; she just knew the Jews had no dealings with them. And Christ answered, “Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst”. The water, the understanding he was going to give her, would bring about the kingdom and salvation for them, because they had been disconnected from it for so long.

precepts.text: Even the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints. It was hid for ages that the northern kingdom had a place in this, to repent and come back. The riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles: the secret that was hid for ages is being revealed; it is no longer gatekept. The apostles were going to go throughout the earth and teach the people that you are not Puerto Rican, you are not Dominican, or whatever name was put on them: you are the children of Israel. And that is what is happening to us now in this present time: the understanding of who we are was hid for ages, but the Lord said in this hour the true worshippers are going to wake up.
precepts.point: Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst, but it shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life. The water, the understanding he was going to give her, would bring about the kingdom and salvation for them, because they were disconnected from it for so long.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
The water Christ gives is “a well of water springing up into everlasting life”, and Paul shows what that understanding is. He is a minister of the gospel “which was preached to every creature which is under heaven”, to fulfil the word of God: “Even the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints”.

It was hid for ages that the northern kingdom had a part to play in this, to repent and come back. The ones who did understand were the learned men who studied, many of them the Pharisees, which is why they said, will he go to the dispersed among the Gentiles and teach them? They read Isaiah, Ezekiel and Deuteronomy. The masses didn't have the scriptures; the learned men had the parchment. But now he gave it to the apostles to teach.

“To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles; which is Christ in you, the hope of glory”. The riches of this mystery among the Gentiles is that the northern kingdom has an opportunity of repentance: he is gathering back the Gentiles. The secret hid for ages is being revealed to the whole world; it is no longer gatekept. The apostles would go throughout the earth and teach the people that you are not Puerto Rican, you are not Dominican, whatever byword was given to you: you are the children of Israel. “Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom”.

That is what is happening to us now. The understanding of this Bible and of who we are was hid for ages, but the Lord said in this hour the true worshippers are going to wake up.

precepts.text: Then Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel in mount Ebal. That is why she said our fathers worshipped in this mountain: when we first came into the land, the first place we came into would have been called Samaria, and the first altars were set up in Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim. When the nation split, the northern kingdom went back up top and worshipped there; but God called his home Jerusalem, where he set up his temple. Notice also: as well the stranger, as he that was born among them; half against mount Gerizim and half against mount Ebal; and the strangers were conversant in the laws of God. When we came into the land we had a mixed multitude among us, and they had to learn the laws; we taught them how to keep the Sabbath day: neither thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor the stranger that is within thy gates.
precepts.point: Ye worship ye know not what: we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews. When he says Jews, he is talking about all Israel. We know what God's will is for us, for his people, and for the nations, and our job is to teach those things, and in teaching them, to gather in one the twelve tribes of Israel.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
The woman at the well said, “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”. On the map, the mountains above the well are Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal. Joshua 8 shows why she said it: “Then Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel in mount Ebal”, “an altar of whole stones, over which no man hath lift up any iron: and they offered thereon burnt offerings unto the Lord, and sacrificed peace offerings.” “And he wrote there upon the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he wrote in the presence of the children of Israel.”

When we first came into the land, the first place we came into was what would be called Samaria, and the first altars were set up in Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim. That is why, when the nation split, the northern kingdom went back up top and worshipped there: this is the place where we worshipped initially. But God called his home Jerusalem; that is where he set up his temple.

Read on: “And all Israel, and their elders, and officers, and their judges, stood on this side the ark and on that side before the priests the Levites, which bare the ark of the covenant of the Lord, as well the stranger, as he that was born among them; half of them over against mount Gerizim, and half of them over against mount Ebal”. The blessings went up on the children of Israel, and the cursing was on Mount Ebal.

“There was not a word of all that Moses commanded, which Joshua read not before all the congregation of Israel, with the women, and the little ones, and the strangers that were conversant among them.” When we came into the land we had a mixed multitude of the other nations among us, and they were conversant in the laws of God. They had to learn the laws. We taught them how to keep the Sabbath day: six days you do your work, and on the seventh no work, neither your manservant, nor your maidservant, nor the stranger that is within thy gates.

Then Christ answered her: “Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father.” There was a time coming, 70 AD, when Jerusalem would be toppled by the Romans, and neither the mountains of Samaria nor Jerusalem would matter, because he was destroying it. His purpose was to gather in one the twelve tribes of Israel.

precepts.text: Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father. Christ told the Samaritan woman the Israelites would not be worshipping in Jerusalem and not in Samaria: he's saying what we read in Luke 21, that we would be carried away as slaves into all nations.
precepts.point: An old map drawn by Esau was shown in class, found by Captain Joel in a library archive: Jewish communities marked all over Africa, the Elephantine Jews, Levite cities in Nigeria, Bnei Ephraim on the slave coast, the Jewish kingdoms of Ganata and Kamnuri, the Berber Jews of the north. Esau knew where we were in Africa; they drew this map to pinpoint us. Why did they need to know where we were? Because slavery was not coincidence. Slavery was war.

note.label: Judgement! To Hell with Your Reparations!

precepts.why:
Christ told the Samaritan woman by the well the same thing he said in Luke 21. She said, “Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet. Our fathers worshipped in this mountain; and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship.” The Samaritans worshipped up on Mount Gerizim, because their fathers used to worship up there back in the days.

“Jesus saith unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father. Ye worship ye know not what”. The Samaritans were not going to worship in that mountain, and the Jews, the Israelites, would not be worshipping at Jerusalem either.

What is Christ saying here? What Luke 21 says: we would “fall by the edge of the sword”, and be “led away captive into all nations”, carried away as slaves into all nations. We fell by the sword in 70 AD, and being led into all nations is a process of time; it didn't all happen in 70 AD. Jerusalem would be “trodden down of the Gentiles”, occupied by heathens, until Christ returns and destroys the Gentiles.

In 70 AD most of us fled into Africa, formed communities, built cities and mingled amongst the Hamitic tribes. Esau drew maps pinpointing where the tribes were all over Africa, the Levite cities of Nigeria, Bnei Ephraim on the slave coast, the Jewish kingdoms, because slavery was not coincidence. Slavery was war.

precepts.point: Christ told her she had five husbands and the man she had now was not her husband. Sex by itself does not make a marriage.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
Christ “must needs go through Samaria”, to Sychar, “near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph”, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh. The woman of Samaria said, “How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” The Samaritans were the northern kingdom, and the Jews had no dealings with them because of that beef from way back.

Hosea is where it came from: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” The Lord said leave them alone, they're joined to idols, and Judah took that as okay: what the hell with them, they're cast off. Yet the woman said, “Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well”? She called Jacob our father, and Joseph's house got that well: she was Israel. She said “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”, Gerizim, where all Israel worshipped before Jerusalem. And Isaiah said “The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel. And all the people shall know, even Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria”, so she said “I know that Messias cometh”.

The disciples “marvelled that he talked with the woman”, because the Jews didn't deal with the northern kingdom. But those are our people. Christ taught the Samaritans two days, and they knew “that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world”: the world is Israel. The dividing hatred said let him alone, but Christ came to heal it.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.”

That is what Joshua meant when he said, serve him “in sincerity and in truth.” To worship in spirit and in truth is to keep what he commanded, not just to say you love the Lord. The ones who say they love him and do none of his commandments are not worshipping him in spirit and in truth.

precepts.text: Christ said, I have meat to eat that you know not of; my meat is to do the will of him that sent me and to finish his work.
precepts.point: Neither has Job gone back from the commandment of his lips; he has esteemed the words of his mouth more than his necessary food. Let us see if Job was moving in the spirit of Christ when he said that.

note.label: Job 23: I Shall Come Forth As Gold

precepts.why:
Job says, “I have esteemed the words of his mouth more than my necessary food.” Was Job moving in the spirit of Christ when he said that? Christ said, “I have meat to eat that ye know not of.” The disciples asked one another whether any man had brought him something to eat, and he answered, “My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work.”

It is the same spirit. Christ's meat was doing the will of the Father; Job esteemed the words of God's mouth more than his necessary food. Regardless of what he was going through, Job kept the commandments: his foot held God's steps, he kept his way and did not decline, and he did not go back from the commandment of his lips. That is why, when he is tried, he comes forth as gold.

precepts.point: Anointed means the smearing of oil, but this goes deeper, into Christ. David was anointed too, but this points to the Messiah who is called Christ.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “For thy servant David’s sake turn not away the face of thine anointed.” Anointed means the smearing of oil, but this goes deeper, into Christ. “The woman saith unto him, I know that Messias cometh, which is called Christ: when he is come, he will tell us all things. precepts.point: He is near to all who call upon Him in truth. Calling upon Him in truth means keeping His commandments.

note.label: Psalm 145: The Greatness and Mercy of the Most High

precepts.why: “The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth.” “God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.” Calling upon him in truth is worshipping him in truth, and that means keeping his commandments.

precepts.text: Jesus himself baptized not, but his disciples.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost is bound to the law. To resist the Holy Ghost is to resist the commandments, and the Comforter brings the words of Christ to remembrance.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
John said plainly, “I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I”, and that one “shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire”. John's water baptism is not the baptism of the one coming after him.

That is why, when the Pharisees heard that Jesus made and baptized more disciples than John, the scripture adds, “Though Jesus himself baptized not, but his disciples”. Christ himself did not baptize with water. Water was John's baptism; Christ's baptism is the Holy Ghost and fire.

precepts.text: The chief of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests, and the Levites, went up to build the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem.
precepts.point: The Jews in that day were Judah, Benjamin and Levi, not all twelve tribes. The Samaritans were Ephraim, and the reason for the separation is written in the prophets.

note.label: John 4: The Woman at the Well and the Nobleman's Son

precepts.why:
The woman of Samaria asked, “How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” The Jews in that day were Judah, Benjamin and Levi, not all twelve tribes. Ezra shows who went back to Jerusalem: “Then rose up the chief of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests, and the Levites, with all them whose spirit God had raised, to go up to build the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem.”

Judah, Benjamin, and the priests and the Levites: those are the Jews. Christ, being a Jew, was of those tribes. The Samaritans were another people, Ephraim, and the reason for the separation is written in the prophets.

precepts.text: Within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people; and the head of Ephraim is Samaria.
precepts.point: The Jews in that day were Judah, Benjamin and Levi, not all twelve tribes. The Samaritans were Ephraim, and the reason for the separation is written in the prophets.

note.label: John 4: The Woman at the Well and the Nobleman's Son

precepts.why:
Isaiah names the Samaritans: “within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people. And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son.”

The head of Ephraim is Samaria. The Samaritans were Ephraim, the northern kingdom, and Ephraim was to be broken within threescore and five years, “that it be not a people.” That is the separation between the Jews, who were Judah, Benjamin and Levi, and the Samaritans, who were Ephraim. It is written in the prophets.

precepts.text: Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.
precepts.point: The Jews in that day were Judah, Benjamin and Levi, not all twelve tribes. The Samaritans were Ephraim, and the reason for the separation is written in the prophets.

note.label: John 4: The Woman at the Well and the Nobleman's Son

precepts.why:
“Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” That is why the Jews had no dealings with the Samaritans. The Samaritans were Ephraim, and Ephraim was joined to idols, and the word was to let him alone.

So the woman's question, “How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria?”, comes out of that history in the prophets: Ephraim broken, joined to idols, let alone by Judah.

precepts.text: Thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and shall not leave in thee one stone upon another.
precepts.point: The true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth. Without temple, sacrifice or priesthood, a scattered people worship in sincerity and in truth, which is what Joshua charged Israel with.

note.label: John 4: The Woman at the Well and the Nobleman's Son

precepts.why:

Christ wept over the city: “If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes.”

“For the days shall come upon thee, that thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side, And shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.”

Not one stone upon another. That is why the hour was coming when men would neither worship in that mountain nor at Jerusalem: the place itself would be laid even with the ground.

precepts.text: Fear the Lord, and serve him in sincerity and in truth.

note.label: John 4: The Woman at the Well and the Nobleman's Son

Serve him in sincerity and in truth. Without temple, sacrifice or priesthood, a scattered people worship in sincerity and in truth, which is what Joshua charged Israel with. Salvation is of the Jews, because Christ sprang out of Judah; and the true worship is not tied to the mountain or to Jerusalem, but is in spirit and in truth, putting away the other gods and serving the Lord.

precepts.text: Jesus made and baptized more disciples than John, though Jesus himself baptized not, but his disciples did, because they had followed John.

When you believe on Christ as the scripture says, rivers of living water flow out of your belly, meaning wisdom and understanding flow out of the mind that consumes and filters information; but that Holy Ghost was not yet given because Jesus was not yet glorified.

Christ himself baptized not with water, but with the Holy Ghost. His disciples baptized with water because they had followed John; two of John's own disciples heard Christ and followed him. That is why in Acts the disciples were still baptizing with water. John decreased and Christ increased, in increments.

The northern tribes had been kept from Jerusalem, the place of sacrifice, and worshipped in their own mountain.
